# Registered KERNEL (type-checking) ceilings, milliseconds.
# Generated by scripts/kernel_cost.py --register on the P0 baseline.
# Ceiling = max(measured x 3.0, 50ms): below the floor,
# timing noise dominates and a ratio would fail on a loaded machine.
#
# ⚠️ Tests.Coverage was RAISED from 777 by P1 BATCH 3, deliberately and not by
# --register (which would have loosened every other line at the same time).
# The module went 378ms -> 1960ms, and 1292ms of that is ONE theorem:
# `mem_dest_claims_are_backed`, which reads the table's SHAPES column — prose,
# up to 75 characters a row — as a character list in the kernel.  It is the gate
# that caught a false `m,r (q)` coverage claim that had stood since batch 1 with
# a reassuring comment beside it.  The cheaper design (a Bool field the renderer
# turns into text) was considered and rejected: it makes the prose unable to
# UNDER-claim while leaving it free to OVER-claim, which is the direction that
# actually failed.  A gate on the artifact costs more than a gate on a shadow of
# it, and this is what the difference costs.  See docs/DECISIONS.md D15.
